correctness.rationale: For connected Cayley graphs, nonlinear-block eigenvalues occur in the regular spectrum with multiplicity divisible by d, while connectedness excludes the only ambiguous case in which all d linear-character sums coincide. Spectral multiplicities modulo d therefore recover the multiset of linear-character sums, and the zero-trace identity then recovers the unique nonlinear character sum. Seitz's Frobenius branch has exactly d linear characters and nonlinear degree d, so AGL(1,q) satisfies the criterion.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. The 2015 source leaves BI-group classification open, while the full 2019 follow-up proves only the order-20 and order-42 affine examples separately and lists BI-groups only through order 30. Targeted searches found no all-q AGL(1,q) BI theorem or equivalent spectral-residue criterion, and no overlapping SCOPE record was found.

value.rationale: The result replaces two isolated affine BI examples by a general spectral mechanism covering every AGL(1,q), and standard CI Sylow restrictions then yield infinitely many nonabelian BI-groups that are not CI-groups.
